_what: Volunteer-built pieces from the Unity museum project (github VRApp), converted with tools/convert_unity_pieces.py. Authorship is from the project's git history: Patrick Molen built the main hall and the modular kit, Kristina Reyes the furnished room and its pieces.

pieces.title: The museum's main hall
pieces.note: The heart of the virtual museum: a courtyard hall with arcades and fountains, where the scanned objects will one day be hung. Everything else in this room is a piece of it.
pieces.hi: This is the museum itself, still being built.

pieces.title: Courtyard fountain, large
pieces.note: The big fountain at the centre of the main hall, tiled in the trim pattern used across the museum.
pieces.hi: Water in the middle of the hall, like a real Tunisian courtyard.

pieces.title: Courtyard fountain, small
pieces.note: The smaller fountain, for the side courts.

pieces.title: Wall with the sign of Tanit
pieces.note: A wall section from the kit carrying the sign of Tanit, the symbol the project takes its name from.
pieces.hi: The sign of Tanit, cut into the museum's own walls.

pieces.title: Palm tree
pieces.note: A palm for the courtyards, so the museum feels like Tunisia and not a white box.
pieces.hi: A palm for the courtyard. It should feel like home.

pieces.title: Carved ceiling
pieces.note: A ceiling piece with carved coffers, for the larger rooms.
pieces.hi: Look up. This goes over your head in the museum.

pieces.title: Clay lamp
pieces.note: A hanging clay lamp that lights the galleries.

pieces.title: Wall lamp
pieces.note: A wall-mounted lamp from the kit.

pieces.hi: A building block. New rooms are puzzled together from these.

pieces.title: Bamboo

pieces.title: Curved bench

pieces.title: Furnished room
pieces.note: A complete furnished room for the virtual museum, built as one piece.
pieces.hi: A whole room, built by hand, ready to hang objects in.

pieces.title: Stained glass lamp

pieces.title: Rug
pieces.note: A rug for the furnished room.

_kit: kit true means a piece of the building itself: an arch, a plain wall, a pillar. They are real work and stay in the archive and on their maker's profile, but they are kept out of the Collection, where an object is shown alone on a plain background and a bare grey arch reads as something broken rather than as a building block.
